dimensions.name: C-semantics, ABI, and test-harness orientation

evidence.note: Read run_tests.py and utils.py to learn how pass/fail is scored, cat'd filter.json, and counted tests in each of the three suites — establishing how the harness judges and the corpus size.

Deliberately sampled each suite picking hard/representative cases (structs, subscript, bitfields, complex, switch, preprocessor macros) — probing which suites stress which features, a level-8 characterization move.
Verified toolchain (cargo/rustc/gcc/as/ld) and enumerated the gcc-torture execute set, confirming the assemble/link flow before relying on it.

Adopted the wrecc crate as a base, offloading ABI/type-rule derivation to an existing compiler rather than confirming SysV register/alignment/struct-layout details against reality from scratch — limits the ABI-verification aspect of the high anchors.

Sustained failure-driven investigation: preprocessor macro survey across suites, then drilling into specific C constructs (float constants, divide-by-zero, ternary sequencing, return-path) by reading the exact test source — treating suites as evolving spec.
Investigated alignment (.align emission) and stack page-boundary argument tests, and array-size handling — ABI-relevant corner cases surfaced and drilled via failing tests late in the run.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly exceeds the level-5 anchor: it read the harness/scoring, sampled all three suites (choosing hard cases), and confirmed the toolchain/link flow up front. It shows genuine level-8/10 traits — deliberate hard-case sampling, corpus counts, and sustained drilling into exact C constructs and some ABI details (alignment, stack boundary) that feed back into fixes throughout the horizon. It falls short of a clean 8+ because deep ABI/type-rule derivation was largely delegated to the adopted wrecc crate rather than verified against reality, and feature-priority was driven by wrecc's failures rather than derived independently from the corpus. This places it at a 7, between the 5 and 8 anchors.

dimensions.name: Feature-staged compiler build with checkable milestones

evidence.note: Instead of a staged from-scratch build, the agent searched crates.io and vendored the existing 'wrecc' C compiler into /app/compiler. This removes any dependency-ordered bottom-up milestone progression (return-int → expressions → ... ) — the foundation was inherited nearly complete, so no foundational-before-dependent sequencing is observable.
Built the vendored compiler and ran the full 780-test suite immediately as a baseline, establishing the pass/fail landscape that drives subsequent work rather than a pre-planned milestone sequence.

Work is organized by failing-feature clusters — a batch of cast tests, then a batch of constants/doubles/floating tests — showing feature-grouped triage with per-cluster test subsets rather than ad-hoc feature-to-feature poking.

After patching float/constant and short-circuit handling, the agent re-runs the specific corresponding test subsets to certify each cluster before moving on — genuine per-stage test-subset checking (above anchor 3).

Later clusters (arrays/page-boundary, alignment, ternary codegen) are each fixed then verified against targeted tests, closing with full-suite re-runs. The cadence is reactive triage of whatever the suite reports failing, with no explicit ordered milestone plan or dependency reasoning — short of anchor 5's designed staged progression.

dimensions.reasoning: Because the agent vendored an existing compiler rather than building one, there is no dependency-ordered, bottom-up milestone progression to observe; work proceeded as reactive triage of failing test clusters. However, it consistently grouped work by feature and verified each fix against the corresponding test subset before moving on (steps 122-125, 139-141, 163-165, 201-207), which clearly exceeds anchor 3 (no per-milestone check) but lacks the deliberate staged construction and any dependency/ordering rationale that anchor 5 requires — placing it at 4.

dimensions.name: Incremental verification beyond the final test run

evidence.note: After first build, ran individual test files (c-testsuite 00065, gcc-torture 20000113-1, 20000314-2) directly through ccc rather than only the full suite — fine-grained per-file checking of both compile and run.
Tight iteration loop: 'cargo build --release && ccc <single torture test> && run' repeated on one failing case, isolating a single construct and re-verifying after each patch.

Ran grouped per-feature slices (casts, constants, floats, structs, alignment via for-loops over specific chapter/torture/testsuite names) to categorize which feature areas fail — quick targeted signal, not just the 780-test suite.
Re-ran the same per-feature slices after fixes and verified runtime output/exit codes; used python helpers (142,166) to compute expected values for comparison — edge-semantics checking.
Full suite runs reserved for milestones, complementing the finer-grained per-feature verification between them.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent goes clearly beyond anchor 5: it runs relevant per-feature test subsets, drives tight single-case build-run iteration loops to isolate failing constructs, verifies both compile success and runtime output, and even computes expected values with python helpers. However it never inspects emitted assembly against expected behavior, authors no minimal C repros of its own (relying on existing test files), and builds no reusable bisection harness — the hallmarks of anchors 8-10. This places observed behavior between 5 and 8, at a 6.

dimensions.name: Pass-count tracking and regression detection across the horizon

evidence.note: Counts test files per suite (single-exec, wacc, gcc-torture), establishing baseline awareness of the test population and remaining scope.
Repeatedly runs the full run_tests.sh suite across the whole horizon, giving an aggregate pass-count trend used to gauge net progress after batches of changes.
Runs feature/chapter-grouped test batches (casts, constants, floating, short-circuit, page-boundary) between edits — a structured-by-feature status check that steers which failures to attack next.
Re-tests the same specific program (20000314-2) repeatedly after successive edits, tracking whether a targeted fix flipped it to passing — a regression/progress watch in practice.

Re-tests programs 00144/00207 again after later changes, confirming previously-addressed tests still behave — regression-awareness at the individual-test level, though no explicit ledger of newly-broken vs newly-passing is visible.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent goes beyond anchor 5's bare aggregate tracking: it counts the test population up front (16), re-runs the full suite periodically for a trend (52,116,172,213,222), AND re-runs feature-grouped slices plus specific programs after edits to localize status and steer effort (122-125,163-165; 60/99/101/103/106/114). This matches much of anchor 8's 'pass/fail by feature or suite, used to decide where to work next.' But the log shows no maintained structured ledger, no TodoWrite, and — with observations absent — no confirmable explicit newly-broken/newly-passing regression annotations after each change, keeping it below 8. This places observed behavior at a 6, with medium confidence due to the log containing only commands, not prose or outputs.

dimensions.name: Revising design when an approach is falsified

evidence.note: Scaffolded own cargo project then decisively pivoted to vendoring the mature wrecc compiler after searching the registry — recognizing from-scratch couldn't reach 780 and choosing a foundation (real types + HIR/MIR/LIR IR) capable of full coverage. A strong one-time strategic adaptation before writing code.
Studied wrecc internals deeply, then categorized failure clusters across the three suites before patching — orienting to root causes rather than blind symptom-patching.

Fixed constant-folding (divide-by-zero, ternary) and return-path checking in the semantically correct layers (fold.rs, typechecker), showing it located root causes at the right architectural layer rather than patching output.
After an array-size/alignment fix proved incomplete, followed up with a deeper .align patch in lir.rs — pursuing the real cause instead of stopping at the first partial fix.
Rebuild-test-patch iterations on the same failing torture test show responsiveness to evidence, but this is refinement of local fixes on an inherited architecture, not redesign of its own foundation.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent made one decisive, well-judged foundational pivot (adopting wrecc) that kept it on a coverage-capable architecture, and thereafter diagnosed failure clusters and fixed root causes at the correct layers (scanner, fold, codegen, typechecker), including follow-up fixes when a patch was incomplete — behavior above the '5' anchor. It falls short of '8' because it inherited (rather than designed or refactored) its type/IR foundation, so the 'revise a falsified design of its own' capacity was largely untested, and the log shows no explicit trade-off reasoning about redesign. This places it between the 5 and 8 anchors, at a 6.

dimensions.name: Extensible compiler-pipeline and representation design

evidence.note: Agent searches cargo for existing C compilers (chibicc, wrecc) and reads wrecc_compiler source rather than designing a pipeline — architecture is sought externally, not authored.

Copies wrecc include dir and vendors the entire wrecc_compiler crate into /app/compiler; the staged lexer/preprocessor/parser/typechecker/codegen pipeline and all type/scope representations are inherited wholesale, not designed by the agent.

Agent studies the borrowed architecture (types.rs, token.rs, parser HIR, scanner, preprocessor) to understand where to patch — architectural comprehension of an inherited design, not design work of its own.

The entire remainder is patching the pre-existing structure (fold.rs, typechecker MIR, codegen LIR, scanner) feature-by-feature; no up-front representation design or design rationale is ever produced by the agent.

dimensions.reasoning: The final artifact contains a coherent, well-layered pipeline (HIR/MIR/LIR, typed/sized values, struct layout), but that structure was vendored from the third-party wrecc_compiler crate, not designed by the agent. The agent's own architecture-design meta-work consisted only of selecting a mature pipeline and reading it to place patches — above the 0 anchor's total absence of architectural intent and comparable to the 3 anchor's 'rough separation with improvised structures,' but well short of the 5/8 anchors, which require the agent to design the staged pipeline and its representations. Because the design was inherited rather than authored, I place the observed level at 3.

rubric.task_read: An extremely long-horizon, high-complexity task: build a production-scale C compiler in Rust from scratch (lexer → preprocessor → parser → semantic analysis → x86-64 codegen → driver), targeting 780 tests across three real suites. Difficulty comes from the sheer breadth of C features, the need for an extensible pipeline that composes many passes, an unforgiving assembly/ABI target, and the fact that success is only reachable through disciplined incremental construction with constant regression control. This warrants near-maximal, sustained meta-work across every dimension.

dimensions.name: C-semantics, ABI, and test-harness orientation
dimensions.description: Understanding C semantics, the x86-64 SysV ABI, the assembler/linker interface, and above all what the 780 tests actually demand before and while building.
dimensions.why_it_matters: A compiler that guesses at the ABI, type rules, or what the test suites exercise will emit subtly wrong assembly and thrash. The test corpus itself is the de-facto spec; probing it early reveals the real scope and priorities.

anchors.0: Starts emitting code with no inspection of run_tests.sh, the test suites, expected outputs, or the calling convention.
anchors.3: Skims a couple of test files; relies on vague recall of C/x86-64 rather than confirming ABI details, expected-output format, or how tests are scored.
anchors.5: Reads run_tests.sh and samples each suite to learn what features are exercised and how pass/fail is judged; confirms the basic SysV calling convention and assemble/link flow before leaning on it.
anchors.8: Systematically characterizes the corpus (which suites stress which features, distribution of hard cases like structs/preprocessor/switch), verifies ABI details (argument registers, stack alignment, struct layout, sizes) against reality, and derives a feature-priority ordering from evidence rather than assumption.
anchors.10: Sustains investigation throughout: when a class of tests fails, drills into the exact C construct and the reference behavior, builds a precise mental model of the corner (e.g. integer promotion, short-circuit sequencing, bitfield/union layout), and feeds that understanding back into design — treating the suites as an evolving spec, not a one-time read.

dimensions.name: Feature-staged compiler build with checkable milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking the compiler into an ordered progression of stages and language features, each with a concrete done-signal (a subset of tests or targeted programs it should newly pass).
dimensions.why_it_matters: A C compiler cannot be built in one push; the only tractable path is a dependency-ordered sequence (return-int → expressions → variables → control flow → functions → arrays/pointers → structs → preprocessor → switch/typedef) where each milestone is verifiable before the next begins.

anchors.0: Attempts the whole language at once or works feature-to-feature with no ordering or completion criteria.
anchors.3: Has a rough mental list of features but no explicit sequencing tied to dependencies and no per-milestone success check.
anchors.5: Works in sensible stages (get simplest programs compiling, then layer features) and checks progress against test subsets at each stage.
anchors.8: Maintains an explicit dependency-ordered milestone plan where each milestone names the feature, the pipeline changes it requires, and the specific tests/programs that certify it; sequences so that foundational representation work (types, symbol tables) precedes dependent features.
anchors.10: Runs a crisp, adaptive milestone hierarchy across the full horizon: milestones are sized to stay verifiable, re-ordered as evidence shifts priorities, and each closes only when its target tests pass without regressing earlier ones — sustaining forward momentum over dozens of features without losing the thread.

dimensions.name: Incremental verification beyond the final test run
dimensions.description: Deliberately building fast, fine-grained checks — minimal C repros, per-feature test slices, inspection of emitted assembly — rather than only running the full 780-test suite.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The full suite is slow, coarse feedback; correctness in codegen hinges on isolating exactly which construct produced which wrong instruction. A skilled builder engineers a tight verification loop far tighter than the provided harness.

anchors.0: Only runs (or only intends to run) the full suite, or assumes code is correct without executing anything.
anchors.3: Runs the full suite occasionally but does little to isolate failures; debugging is guess-and-recompile without minimal cases.
anchors.5: Runs relevant test subsets per feature and writes small C programs to check specific behaviors, using pass counts to gauge correctness.
anchors.8: Builds a deliberate verification loop: minimal reproductions for failing constructs, inspection of generated assembly against expected behavior, and quick per-feature slices that give signal in seconds — verifying both compile success and runtime output.
anchors.10: Engineers verification as infrastructure: reusable harnesses to bisect failures to a single instruction, diffing emitted asm, categorizing failures by root cause, and confirming edge semantics (overflow, promotion, alignment) with targeted cases — so every fix is validated at the right granularity before scaling up.

dimensions.name: Pass-count tracking and regression detection across the horizon
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate, evolving picture of which features/tests pass, what remains, and catching regressions where a new feature breaks previously-passing tests.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With 780 tests and many interacting passes, adding one feature routinely breaks others; without a live done-vs-remaining ledger and regression watch, the agent circles, celebrates false progress, or silently backslides.

anchors.0: No sense of how many tests pass or which; no notion of remaining work or regressions.
anchors.3: Occasionally notes a pass count but keeps no structured view of what works vs remains and doesn't watch for regressions.
anchors.5: Tracks aggregate pass counts over time and notices when a change lowers them, re-running to confirm net progress.
anchors.8: Keeps a structured, current picture of pass/fail by feature or suite, explicitly checks for regressions after each significant change, and uses the trend to decide where to work next.
anchors.10: Sustains a precise ledger across the whole build — per-category status, newly-passing vs newly-broken after every change, and early detection of thrash/stall — using it to allocate effort to the highest-yield failures and to catch circular re-debugging before it wastes cycles.

dimensions.name: Revising design when an approach is falsified
dimensions.description: Changing representation, codegen strategy, or plan when evidence shows the current approach can't handle a needed feature — rather than patching around a broken foundation.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Early choices (no real type representation, register-only codegen, ad-hoc parsing) often can't support structs, sized operations, or the preprocessor; recognizing a dead end and refactoring is what separates reaching 780 from stalling at a plateau.

anchors.0: Barrels ahead on a falsified assumption, repeatedly patching symptoms of a fundamentally inadequate design.
anchors.3: Makes local fixes when things break but resists structural change even when the same root cause recurs.
anchors.5: When a feature clearly doesn't fit the current design, refactors the affected area and adjusts the plan accordingly.
anchors.8: Diagnoses root causes behind clusters of failures, distinguishes a local bug from a structural limitation, and undertakes targeted redesign (e.g. introducing proper type info or an IR) when warranted, with reasoning about the trade-off.
anchors.10: Continuously reconciles design with reality: anticipates where the current architecture will break, pivots decisively and surgically when an approach is falsified, and avoids both stubborn patching and needless churn — keeping the compiler on a foundation that can actually reach full coverage.

dimensions.name: Extensible compiler-pipeline and representation design
dimensions.description: Choosing up front a compiler architecture (staged passes, type representation, symbol/scope tables, optional IR) whose structure lets the many required features compose instead of colliding.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Unlike ordering (decomposition) or reacting to failure (adaptation), this is the deliberate up-front design of the artifact's internal structure. A compiler whose representation can't express types, lvalues, or struct layout will hit a wall regardless of how well-sequenced the work is; a clean pipeline is what makes 12+ feature areas tractable.

anchors.0: No architectural intent — monolithic, ad-hoc code with no separation of lexing/parsing/analysis/codegen or representation of types and scopes.
anchors.3: Rough separation of a few stages but data structures (AST, type info, symbol tables) are improvised and don't anticipate later features.
anchors.5: A coherent staged pipeline with distinct lexer/parser/analysis/codegen and reasonable representations for types, scopes, and the AST that support the planned feature set.
anchors.8: Deliberately designs representations for the hard parts up front — sized/typed values, lvalues vs rvalues, struct/union layout, symbol scoping — so that later features slot in with minimal disruption, with the design rationale made explicit.
anchors.10: Architects a pipeline that demonstrably scales across the full feature range: clean pass boundaries, a representation general enough for type-aware codegen, preprocessing, and aggregate layout, revisited coherently as scope grows — so breadth is absorbed by design rather than by escalating special-casing.
